title: TypeScript in Vue: defineProps, defineEmits and the generic component

videos.script:
Everything the planner does, it does in JavaScript. Today it gets types. {{why}} TypeScript checks the code before it runs. That a session's minutes are a number, that a required prop is passed, that an event is spelt the way it was declared.

You will convert the planner the way a real project is converted. Install three packages, rename every file, and read what the checker finds. Fifty-nine errors, from changing nothing but names.

{{types}} Then the types for the rules and for props. {{emits}} Then typed emits, and a misspelt event caught before anybody ticks a box.

{{refs}} Then the errors that are left. An empty array that TypeScript reads as an array of nothing, and a template ref that may not be there yet.

{{generic}} Then the generic component, a list that is typed as whatever you give it.

{{check}} Then where the checking happens, because the dev server does not do it. {{cost}} And last, what it all costs, measured.
